decisions.reason: Flagship electrometer close to the core dosimetry business is featured on the home page in both years, signaling results at or above aspiration with no trigger for search.
Risk management software builds on the established QA offer and has kept its own page for two years, and an expanding firm has enough slack to carry its still uncertain results.
CT phantom extends the core imaging QA line and fits the flagship imaging direction, so there is little reason to drop it.
Mammography phantom is distant from the core offer, but it is new and backed by the imaging QA focus and expansion slack, so the firm likely gives it more time before judging it against aspirations.
Full field mammography phantom overlaps with Product D and is distant from the core, which makes it a candidate for consolidation, yet slack and the strategic imaging push favor keeping it for now.
Flagship imaging QA instrument line central to the firm's stated direction is very unlikely to be withdrawn.
